correctness.rationale: For n=p+1, D_p is one row d, so Sherman–Morrison gives S=I-alpha d^T d with alpha=lambda/(1+lambda*binom(2p,p)). Factoring d=v^T D yields the onto-gradient induced operator I-alpha u v^T. Each diagonal stays positive because alpha*u_j*v_j<1; its maximum absolute column sum is 1+alpha M_p, attained by the unique-jump step. M_1=-2, M_2=0, M_p>0 for p>=3 (j=0), and the central binomial bounds plus Stirling prove M_p/binom(2p,p)->sqrt(2). Exact rational inversion independently matched all step norms for p=1..8, lambda=1/11 and 3/4; that finite check does not prove the limit.
